newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Banks agree to suspend covenants on NZ's Maine.
newsitem.headline: Banks agree to suspend covenants on NZ's Maine.

text.p: The principal shareholder in Skellerup New Zealand Ltd, Maine Investments Ltd, said on Tuesday it was making positive progress towards restructuring the investment company and gaining an associated NZ$40 million additional equity and financial support from shareholders.
Syndicated banks supporting Maine had also agreed to suspend various financial covenants, it said in a statement.

An outline of the proposal developed by Maine in conjunction with its principal shareholders and representatives of the company's senior bank syndicate was formally presented to Maine's entire bank syndicate on June 25.
Maine said they had all indicated preliminary support of the plan and would seek approvals from their respective institutions.
No changes to the junior bondholders' debt are contemplated.

"Maine believes the restructure and funding injection will be beneficial to all employees, suppliers, customers, senior lenders and bondholders," said Maine spokesman Murray Bolton, who led a leveraged management buyout of Skellerup last year.
Maine, owned by U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs and Skellerup managers, bought Skellerup for NZ$400 million.
Skellerup is a diversified investment group including retail chains Levenes and Palmers Garden.
The heavily debt-financed takeover ran into problems, which saw yields on the 10 percent Skellerup bonds jump to 35 percent.
The bonds were initially issued in March 1996 with a yield of 10 percent and last traded at 22 percent.
Four local institutions hold most of the NZ$77 million bonds on issue NZSFL08011000=NZ.
Maine said the suspension of the covenants did not affect Maine's debt servicing obligations which it continues to meet.

On June 20 Maine's shareholders agreed to contribute up to NZ$40 million in additional equity and financial support to the company, provided associated rearrangements could be agreed with the banking syndicate.
